question: Visualize the p-value and effect size (log2FC) distributions from the provided MeRIP-seq and proteomic data, and perform a chi-square test to evaluate the association between m6A modification status and differential gene expression using the m6A status and DEG status columns already provided in the MeRIP-seq data.

files.eval_guideline: The chi-square p-value must match the reference within two orders of magnitude; whitespace and numeric formatting may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Identical filenames and .txt formats indicate the chi-square test p-value output for the association between provided m6A and DEG statuses.
files.strategy_reasoning: The output is a single numeric chi-square p-value, so numeric comparison handles whitespace and numeric formatting differences. An RAE tolerance of 99 permits values up to 100 times the reference, although it cannot enforce the symmetric lower bound implied by two orders of magnitude.

files.eval_guideline: 2x2 panel figure with log2FC on x-axis; the three individual panels (top-left, top-right, bottom-left) are single-dataset histograms with frequency/count on the y-axis, while the bottom-right panel is an overlaid normalized density comparison of all three datasets (y-axis is density, not frequency); panel labels, colors, bin sizes, and fonts may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Identical filenames and .png image formats clearly correspond to the requested effect size (log2FC) distribution visualization.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual verification of a 2×2 figure with three individual log2FC count histograms and an overlaid normalized density comparison of all three datasets in the bottom-right panel. Semantic comparison checks these structural and axis requirements while allowing differences in labels, colors, bins, and fonts.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images use a 2x2 layout containing individual log2FC histograms for proteomic, m6A methylation, and gene expression data, plus an overlay of all three datasets. The individual histograms show similar qualitative patterns: proteomic values have a broad central distribution, m6A values concentrate slightly above zero, and gene expression has a sharp peak near zero with long tails. Differences in bin widths plausibly explain much of the variation in histogram peak counts; exact data identity cannot be established visually. The critical discrepancy is the bottom-right panel: the reference overlays normalized probability densities, whereas the candidate overlays raw frequencies and explicitly labels its y-axis Frequency. Because the candidate reports 3,850 proteomic observations versus 12,754 observations for each other dataset, its overlay strongly reflects unequal sample sizes and makes the proteomic curve appear much smaller. This changes the interpretation of relative distribution shapes and fails the explicit density-comparison requirement. The candidate also omits the reference's zero-change reference lines, although that is a minor difference. Colors, outline versus filled histograms, fonts, and shared axis limits do not materially affect equivalence. Neither figure contains p-value distributions or chi-square results, so those broader task components cannot be assessed from these effect-size figures.

The individual panels use counts and show closely matching qualitative patterns: proteomic p-values concentrate near zero and decline toward one; m6A p-values have a strong near-zero peak and a relatively flat background; gene expression p-values peak near zero and one, with counts generally increasing toward one across the interior. The critical discrepancy is the bottom-right panel: the reference overlays normalized probability densities, whereas the candidate overlays raw frequency histograms, explicitly labeled Frequency. Because the candidate reports 3,850 proteomic observations versus 12,754 observations for each other dataset, its combined panel confounds distribution shape with sample size and visually suppresses the proteomic distribution. This changes the cross-dataset comparison and violates the explicit density requirement. The candidate therefore preserves most individual-distribution content but is only partially equivalent.
